newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Big roll in Morris, techs busy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Big roll in Morris, techs busy.

text.p: An investor rolled a large call position in Philip Morris Cos Inc options from the June series to the January 1998 series on Tuesday.
The June 26-5/8 call, with open interest of 14,764 contracts, traded 14,667 by Monday afternoon. The January 30 call, which had open interest of 16,025, traded 16,436 contracts.
"It looks like they're rolling 99 percent of the June 26-5/8s into January," said Michael Schwartz, a managing director at Oppenheimer & Co.
Philip Morris shares were down 1/2 at 42-1/4.
Elsewhere, options on technology stocks led most trading as the underlying shares continued to move sharply, mostly lower.
In the group, Intel Corp, Seagate Technology Inc, International Business Machines Corp, Compaq Computer Corp, Cisco Systems Inc and Quantum Corp all posted heavy losses.
Intel fell four to 145-3/4, Seagate lost 3-1/4 to 39-1/8 and IBM dropped two to 85-1/8. Also, Compaq shed 5-7/8 to 101-3/4, Cisco lost 2-7/16 to 65-3/8 and Quantum was down 1-3/8 at 38-1/2.
Weakness in the group contributed to a steep drop in the Nasdaq composite index, which was down 17.34 points, or around 1.25 percent, at 1,387.45.
Options traders said order flows were largely two-way but that with the stocks down, put options drew more attention but not necessarily more volume.
At the American Stock Exchange, the Seagate June 40 put was the most active, with volume of about 4,450 contracts. It was up 1-5/16 at 2-1/2. Open interest was 5,677.
The IBM July 65 put, with volume of about 2,140 contracts, was the most active equity put at the Chicago Board Options Exchange but not the most active IBM option.
That distinction went to the June 90 call, with turnover of roughly 3,260 contracts.
Some traders said activity overall was on the sluggish side as investors began to move to the sidelines ahead of the key May U.S. employment report, which is scheduled for release on Friday.
